scheme_name: Central Silk Board – Bivoltine Silk Development Programme
overview: The Central Silk Board – Bivoltine Silk Development Programme is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, aimed at enhancing bivoltine silk production through research, extension, seed production, cocoon production practices, marketing, credit facilitation, policy options, and stakeholder participation. It was formulated during the XII Five Year Plan (2012-13 to 2016-17) with the goal of increasing bivoltine silk production from 1685 MT to 5000 MT, representing a 197% increase. The programme focuses on mulberry sector development and includes the formation of 179 clusters across India to promote large-scale bivoltine sericulture, particularly targeting economically weaker sections in rural areas.
objectives: Enhance bivoltine silk (3A grade and above) production from 1685 MT to 5000 MT
Formulate about 179 clusters all over India for bivoltine sericulture promotion
Promote import substitute bivoltine silk generation
Generate employment particularly for economically weaker sections in rural areas
Strengthen research, extension, seed production, cocoon production practices, marketing, credit facilitation, policy options, and stakeholder participation in decision-making
eligibility: The programme targets stakeholders in the sericulture sector, including farmers and reelers, particularly from economically weaker sections in rural areas, with a focus on mulberry sector development for bivoltine silk production. Specific eligibility criteria are not explicitly detailed in the evidence, but the scheme is implemented through state governments and involves stakeholder participation in decision-making areas.
benefits: Benefits include increased bivoltine silk production, enhanced income for stakeholders through improved productivity and quality, employment generation in rural areas, technology transfer from R&D units, and support for cluster-based sericulture development. The scheme facilitates access to improved mulberry varieties, package of practices, silkworm breeds (CSR2 x CSR4, CSR4 x CSR5, CSR18 x CSR19), improved rearing methodology, disease management, and reeling technologies suitable for tropical climates.
financial_support: Financial support is provided through the Catalytic Development Programme (CDP) under the Central Sector Scheme, with funding allocated for research, extension, seed production, cocoon production practices, marketing, credit facilitation, policy options, and increased stakeholder participation. The scheme leverages Central Sector Schemes of the Central Silk Board, with financial assistance structured as subsidies for beneficiary-oriented components, though specific quantum per entity is not detailed in the evidence.
application_process: The application process is not explicitly detailed in the evidence. However, the scheme is implemented through state governments, and proposals are likely submitted by state sericulture departments or implementing agencies to the Central Silk Board for consideration, approval, and funding, following guidelines similar to other Central Sector Schemes involving project formulation, baseline surveys, and submission to state directorates.
implementing_agency: Central Silk Board, Ministry of Textiles, Government of India
caveats: The programme was formulated during the XII Five Year Plan (2012-13 to 2016-17) and may not be currently active
Implementation is dependent on state government participation and fund allocation
Focus is primarily on the mulberry sector for bivoltine silk promotion
